DISCLAIMER: I DO NOT Agree with raising the pay for fast food to $15.

However, the argument isnt that they deserve the money becasue the job is hard or becasue they are skilled. Thats a strawman thats been thrown out every time this comes up. The argument is actually that they want the wage increase so they can actually afford to have a home while working in fast food. Which is still stupid, just not quite as stupid.

Every person I know that has woked fast food understands that they dont have a difficult or exclusive job, but they also would have to work three of those jobs in order to be able to afford things like a mortgage, kids, and a car payment. Basically, they want to be able to live a normal life while working at McDonald's which is impossible right now. Its not an insane thing to ask for but I think its fine to tell them no.

They want fast food to be a career, but its not. Fast food is what you do on the side while you learn a skill that will become a career. You dont start a family on a fast food job. But thats what they want to be able to do. It makes a kind of sense. Its still wrong and dumb, but its not asinine like 'omg burgers r hard so pay me mor'

Some of them think it for no further reason than that's what they've been told by the people who make careers out of manipulating the poor and uneducated.. Some of them think it because they know life for them is horrible and frustrating, with no way ahead in life for them, and they feel it shouldn't be that way, but they genuinely don't know of any other answers. Call them less-driven, uneducated, or just unlucky, but they still look around and see those getting paid more (for whatever reasons), and those people's lives don't look so devastatingly horrible, so they wonder why can't something be done for them, too? It's probably very true that you took the initiative they did not and bettered yourself; working hard to make smart, often painfully strict, financial choices, so that you didn't have to rely on unskilled labor jobs, but looking down on a person who does work you're not willing to do is a bad on you, not them (no matter how much they should be paid).
